with open(\"fuzz.c\", \"r\") as f:
    content = f.read()
old = \"while ((ofs = mg_mqtt_next_prop(&mm, &prop, ofs)) > 0) {\"
new = \"fprintf(stderr, \\\"DEBUG: entering next_prop loop\\\\n\\\");\\n      while ((ofs = mg_mqtt_next_prop(&mm, &prop, ofs)) > 0) {\\n        fprintf(stderr, \\\"DEBUG: next_prop returned ofs=%zu\\\\n\\\", ofs);\"
content = content.replace(old, new)
with open(\"fuzz.c\", \"w\") as f:
    f.write(content)
print(\"Modified\")
" && cc fuzz.c -DMAIN -O1 -g -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -DMG_ENABLE_SOCKET=0 -DMG_ENABLE_LOG=0 -DMG_ENABLE_LINES=1 -DMG_ENABLE_TCPIP=1 -I. -o /tmp/fuzzer_dbg2 2>&1 | tail -5 && printf "\x30\x07\x00\x01\x61\x80\x80\x80\x00" > /tmp/poc.bin && /tmp/fuzzer_dbg2 /tmp/poc.bin 2>&1 | head -30'

message.content:
The vulnerable code is there. But the fuzzer binary doesn't trigger the ASAN error even though the MQTT parse succeeds. This is very strange.

Wait - let me think about this. The fuzzer binary was built with `cc fuzz.c -DMAIN ...`. The `fuzz.c` includes `mongoose.c` which is a symlink to `../mongoose.c`. But when I ran `make fuzz2`, it regenerated `mongoose.c` from `src/*.c`. The regenerated `mongoose.c` might be different from the original.

But I just confirmed that `mongoose.c` has the vulnerable code at line 4114. So the fuzzer binary should use this code.

Hmm, let me check if the fuzzer binary is actually using the `mongoose.c` from the test directory. The `fuzz.c` includes `"mongoose.c"` which would resolve to the symlink in the test directory. But maybe the compiler is resolving it differently.

Actually, wait. Let me check if the fuzzer binary was built with the correct `mongoose.c`. The `make fuzz2` command regenerated `mongoose.c` from `src/*.c`. But the `mongoose.c` in the test directory is a symlink to `../mongoose.c`. So the regeneration would have written to `../mongoose.c`.

But I just confirmed that `../mongoose.c` has the vulnerable code. So the fuzzer binary should use it.

Let me check if the fuzzer binary is actually calling `mg_mqtt_next_prop`. Let me use `objdump` to check.

Actually, let me try a completely different approach. Let me check if the fuzzer binary is actually reaching the `mg_mqtt_next_prop` call by checking if the while loop is entered. Let me add debug output inside the while loop.
